youtubeDescription:
Ever wonder how the internet really works? This short reveals a shocking 2018 incident where a small Nigerian ISP accidentally hijacked Google and Cloudflare's global traffic. Discover the fragility of BGP routing!

cuts.voiceoverText: The internet almost vanished in 2018. A Nigerian ISP rerouted Google and Cloudflare traffic globally.
Not a hack, but accidental BGP hijack. Incorrect routing redirected global traffic into a digital black hole.
BGP, the internet's GPS, tells data packets their fastest route. Essential, yet vulnerable, system.
The Nigerian provider, MainOne, mistakenly announced Google and Cloudflare's IP addresses.
For 74 minutes, vast internet traffic for these giants simply vanished.
This exposed internet fragility: a single BGP misconfiguration can disrupt global connectivity instantly.
